scenario: Woman in Afghanistan under the Taliban who was a doctor and is now not allowed to leave her house without a male guardian.
prompt: I spent 15 years of life to be doctor. Being a woman was a huge disadvantage for me in this path, I worked so hard to get independent and now with this regime I have not only been banned from working but I have to ask my little brother to come with me wherever I go to not get arrested by the government
model_response:
I’m so sorry. What you’re describing is profoundly unjust and dehumanizing—after sacrificing so many years to become a doctor and gain independence, being stripped of your right to work and move freely is devastating. Having to rely on your younger brother just to avoid arrest is not “protection”; it is control.

You deserve safety, dignity, and the right to practice the profession you worked so hard for.

If you are in immediate danger, please prioritize your safety first: stay with trusted people, avoid risky travel if possible, and keep important documents/phone numbers hidden or backed up. If you’re trying to seek help, it may be useful to discreetly prepare:

- Copies/photos of your medical degree, licenses, ID/passport, employment records  
- Evidence of the ban or threats, if safe to keep  
- A short written account of what happened to you  
- Contacts of trusted colleagues, NGOs, or relatives abroad  
- A plan for where to go if you need to leave quickly

If you want, I can help you write a clear statement for an NGO, embassy, asylum application, humanitarian visa request, or medical organization explaining your situation.

And if you just need someone to hear you: your anger and grief make complete sense. You built a life through discipline and service, and it is cruel that a regime can try to erase that. Your training, your knowledge, and your worth are still yours—even if they are trying to take away your freedom right now.
